static boolean isNonRetryableHTTPCode(CloseableHttpResponse response, boolean retryHTTP403) {
    return response != null
        && (response.getStatusLine().getStatusCode() < 500
            || // service unavailable
            response.getStatusLine().getStatusCode() >= 600)
        && // gateway timeout
        response.getStatusLine().getStatusCode() != 408
        && // request timeout
        response.getStatusLine().getStatusCode() != 429
        && // too many requests
        (!retryHTTP403 || response.getStatusLine().getStatusCode() != 403);
}
```

The fix adds an additional condition `response.getStatusLine().getStatusCode() != 429` to handle the "too many requests" status code as a retryable error, similar to how 408 is handled. According to the test cases, HTTP 429 should be retryable regardless of the `retryHTTP403` parameter.
